headline: Proposed Portland train station move to St. John Street discussed; options for a future resolution outlined.
summary: The Northern New England Passenger Rail Authority wants to move Portland's train station from Thompson's Point to a site on St. John Street, near Barber Foods and the Metro bus garage. The project would cost about $60 million, with a $48 million federal grant and at least $12 million sought from the state. City staff favored a different location, site two near Union Station Plaza.
discussion: Station site: Speakers compared the St. John Street site with Union Station Plaza on safety, walking access, bus connections, and property owner concerns.
Funding and cost: Some asked whether the $12 million state match would take money from other transit and safety projects. NEPRA said funding rail does not mean cutting bus funding.
Maine Health and county land: Questions focused on whether Maine Health and Cumberland County would sell or give up land for site two. Officials said both have said no.
Rail crossing safety: NEPRA said gates would stay down longer at sites closer to Congress Street. Ambulance access to the hospital was raised as a concern.
Next steps: Staff laid out three options for a future resolution: keep the station at Thompson's Point, support site two, or support site three with conditions.
